heroSub: Eight budget Loei stays we've reviewed in depth, all scoring 8.0 and up — from a Loei-city guesthouse under ฿500 a night and a roomy budget hotel in the city centre, to a garden guesthouse near the Chiang Khan walking street, a wooden hostel on the Mekong, and a small pool villa and container resort by the river. Starting from around ฿300–1,200/night.
introH2: 🏔️ Can you do Loei on a budget, and which area gives the best value?
introHtml: Loei is known for its Mekong-side resorts and mountain views, but the province has more well-rated stays in the low-hundreds-to-low-thousands range than most people expect — in-town guesthouses, roomy budget hotels, a house in a garden, a wooden riverside hostel, and even a small pool villa and a container resort by the river. The key to doing Loei on a budget is to match your area to your plan, because the budget stays cluster in two main zones. Chiang Khan sits on the Mekong, about 50 km from Loei city, with its old-wood walking street, dawn sticky-rice alms and the Kaeng Khut Khu rapids. And Loei city is the central base, close to the airport and shops, good for driving out to Chiang Khan, Phu Ruea or Dan Sai on day trips. The mountain zones like Phu Ruea and Dan Sai are mostly pricier resorts, so they aren't in this budget list. This guide rounds up 8 budget Loei stays we've reviewed, all scoring 8.0 and up — each read from real guest reviews, with the honest upsides and caveats, prices compared on 3 sites, and direct booking links.
mrtHtml: Loei has no metro and little public transport — renting a car or motorbike is by far the most practical option, especially for getting between Chiang Khan and the city. Within Loei city you'll find a few songthaews and motorbike taxis, though they're hard to flag down in the evening. Loei Airport (LOE) is about 10 minutes from the city and around an hour from Chiang Khan. The budget zones in this guide: Chiang Khan — the Mekong, the walking street, Kaeng Khut Khu, sticky-rice alms (Baan Suan La Moon, Suneta Hostel, Friends House, With A View let you walk the walking-street quarter, while INBOX sits on the river out of town and needs a car) · Loei city — the central base near the airport and shops (King Hotel, Sugar Guesthouse, Loei Village). In-town Loei has few sights of its own; most people use it as a base to drive out around the province.

entries.storyHtml: The best value in this list starts at just ฿750, yet posts the highest score of the set at 9.1 across 344 reviews — Baan Suan La Moon is a house in a leafy fruit garden near the Chiang Khan walking street, an easy walk to the walking street and the Mekong. Real reviews praise the cleanliness, the quiet garden setting, and an owner who looks after guests personally, warm as family and full of good food and sightseeing tips; rooms have AC and a fridge, and there are free bikes and free parking. The honest caveats: it's a small guesthouse of about 6 rooms with no pool, the rooms don't have Mekong views, there's no lift, and breakfast is simple and not always served — check first. It's the best fit for anyone who wants a quiet garden-house feel near Chiang Khan's old town on a budget.

entries.storyHtml: The cheapest in-town option in Loei, yet it scores a strong 8.9 — King Hotel Loei starts at just ฿550 on Chum Sai Road in the heart of the city, a 5–7 minute walk to the walking street and night market, near a 7-Eleven and eateries. What's surprising at this price: rooms are fairly roomy, many with a private balcony, plus a central Thai-Japanese garden, free parking and a lift. Real reviews praise the value, the central location, the room size and friendly staff. It's the best fit for budget travellers who want a roomy central base for driving out around the province.

entries.storyHtml: A boutique hostel where you sleep in an old wooden house right on the Mekong walking street — Suneta Hostel Chiangkhan scores 8.9 across 206 reviews, with budget no-window rooms from ฿700 and Mekong river-view rooms with a balcony over the Lao bank from around ฿1,400. The selling point is a location on the walking street where you can walk to everything, an old wooden house full of character, free breakfast, bikes to borrow, and an easy walk to the dawn sticky-rice alms. The honest caveats: it's a wooden house, so sound carries and floorboards creak in some rooms, the cheap no-window rooms can feel stuffy, storage is limited, and there's no pool. It's the best fit for couples and travellers who want to soak up genuine riverside life on the walking street on a budget.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: For a river view and a balcony, pick a River View room (around ฿1,400); if you're keeping it cheap, the ฿700 no-window room still does the job. entries.storyHtml: The cheapest stay in the list, starting at just ฿300 — Sugar Guesthouse is a backpacker guesthouse in Loei city, scoring 8.8 across 17 reviews, set on a quiet lane yet a 5-minute walk to the market and the river. What travellers love: the owner is warm and speaks fluent English, genuinely helpful with where to go and how to get there around Loei, rents motorbikes and bikes and arranges transfers, with a garden, a sala to lounge in, a shared kitchen and free tea and coffee. The honest caveats: the cheapest rooms are upstairs fan rooms with a shared bathroom — for a private bathroom pick a downstairs room — the soundproofing is thin, and it's a budget guesthouse with no pool or lift. It's the best fit for solo travellers or backpackers using Loei city as a base to head out.

entries.storyHtml: A city boutique in Loei that punches above its price thanks to a breakfast everyone talks about — Loei Village Hotel scores 9.0 across 80 reviews, from ฿900/night. What reviews single out is the daily-changing breakfast buffet, heavy on Thai and local dishes; rooms are clean and spacious for a 3-star, some with a balcony over the city and sunset, and it sits on a quiet lane so you sleep well. There's free parking, EV charging, bikes to borrow and a 24-hour front desk that can arrange airport transfers. The honest caveats: it's down a lane, so it's a 10–15 minute walk to the main city centre, the soundproofing between rooms is thin, and the building has no lift. It's the best fit for those who want a clean, quiet in-town boutique at an accessible price.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: Don't miss the daily-changing breakfast, and the Deluxe City View has a balcony and is noticeably larger than the Superior. If stairs are hard for you, ask for a lower floor, since the building has no lift.

entries.storyHtml: If you want a pool on a budget in Chiang Khan, this delivers — Friends House is a small loft-style pool villa in concrete and wood in central Chiang Khan, scoring 8.6 across 105 reviews, from ฿900/night. The highlight reviews mention is the saltwater pool and a kids' pool, which are rare at this price in Chiang Khan; with few rooms the pool never feels crowded, almost like a semi-private one, and rooms are clean and well-equipped with a wide, wet-and-dry bathroom, quiet and private. The honest caveats: there's no breakfast and no on-site restaurant, so you head out to eat; it isn't right on the Mekong, so there's no river view from the rooms; it's about 1.3 km from the walking street; and with so few rooms it's hard to book in high season. It's the best fit for couples and small families who want a quiet, semi-private pool on a budget.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: For a room near the pool pick a Pool Corner, but book ahead as rooms are few. There's no breakfast, so plan to head out to Chiang Khan town, which you can reach by bike. Check-out is fairly early (around 11:00–11:30), so allow for it.

entries.storyHtml: A Mekong-side container-concept resort that's the most-reviewed in this list with 550 reviews — INBOX Living Rimkhong scores 8.0, from ฿750/night, set on the Mekong at Bu Hom. The draw is the colourful container rooms that photographers love, open Mekong and Lao-bank mountain views wider than in town, beanbag balconies for sunset, BBQ grills for grilling by the water, and a free in-room minibar — good for groups and families. The honest caveats: it's about 6 km from the Chiang Khan walking street with no shops in walking distance, so you really need a car; rooms are small as containers go and not for heavy luggage; and there's no on-site restaurant, with a simple breakfast. It's the best fit for those with a car who want a quiet riverside stay and good photos, not in-town strolling.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: For the fullest river view, pick a front-row Riverside room. You'll need a car, and buy food and water in town first, as there are no shops within walking distance. For a group, book a BBQ grill by the water for the atmosphere.

The selling point is a location where you step out the door onto the walking street, an old wooden house decorated in wood tones that suit the old town, an in-house cafe and homemade bakery whose breakfast draws plenty of praise, and upper-floor River View rooms over the Mekong and the Lao bank. faqTitle: FAQ — Common traveller questions about budget Loei hotels

faq.q: ❓ Which budget Loei stay is the best value?
faq.a: On value (score per baht), Baan Suan La Moon ฿750, scoring 9.1 across 344 reviews, is the best value in this list — the highest score, heavily reviewed, and cheap. For the cheapest possible, Sugar Guesthouse from ฿300 (an in-town guesthouse) and King Hotel Loei ฿550 (a roomy budget hotel scoring 8.9) are great value.

faq.q: ❓ How much do budget Loei hotels cost?
faq.a: In this guide, from about ฿300–1,200 a night · At the lightest: Sugar Guesthouse from ฿300 (fan room), King Hotel ฿550, Suneta Hostel from ฿700 (no-window room) · Garden and in-town stays: Baan Suan La Moon and INBOX ฿750, Loei Village and Friends House ฿900 · And a wooden house on the Mekong walking street, With A View, from ฿1,200 · All are approximate starting rates outside peak season; the cool season and long weekends push them up clearly.

faq.q: ❓ Which area should I stay in to do Loei on a budget?
faq.a: Loei's budget stays cluster in two zones · Chiang Khan, on the Mekong, suits the walking street, sticky-rice alms and Kaeng Khut Khu (Baan Suan La Moon, Suneta Hostel, Friends House, With A View let you walk the quarter, while INBOX sits on the river ~6 km out and needs a car) · Loei city works as a central base near the airport for driving out to Chiang Khan, Phu Ruea and Dan Sai (King Hotel, Sugar, Loei Village) · Chiang Khan and the city are about 50 km apart, so plan your zone before booking.

faq.q: ❓ Do I need a vehicle to do Loei on a budget?
faq.a: If you stay in the Chiang Khan walking-street quarter you can walk around it (Suneta, With A View, Baan Suan La Moon) · But to get between Chiang Khan and Loei city (about 50 km) or up to Phu Ruea/Dan Sai, a vehicle is close to essential, as public transport is very limited · Out-of-town riverside stays like INBOX (~6 km from the walking street) and the in-town Loei stays also suit people with a car · Renting a car or motorbike is the most practical and flexible option (Sugar Guesthouse can help arrange rentals and transfers).

faq.q: ❓ Are there budget Loei stays with a pool?
faq.a: Yes · Friends House ฿900 in Chiang Khan has a saltwater pool and a kids' pool, rare at this price; with few rooms the pool never feels crowded, almost semi-private · The lighter-budget stays (guesthouses, hostels, riverside resorts) mostly have no pool and lean on location and atmosphere instead · If you want a 4-star hotel with a pool in Loei city, see our Top 10 Loei Hotels guide (Loei Palace).

faq.q: ❓ Which site is cheapest for booking Loei hotels?
faq.a: Prices on each site (Agoda, Booking.com, Trip.com) differ by promotion and period, so open all 3 to compare before every booking — 7 of the 8 stays here compare fully across all 3 sites, while Sugar Guesthouse's Trip.com link is a search page and books directly on Agoda and Booking.com · Each review page in this article gives you the price-comparison links, which can save tens to a few hundred baht a night.
